meta.title: Clinical Skills OSCE Stations
meta.description: 6 OSCE stations for clinical skills practice covering emergency medicine, cardiology, neurology, and respiratory

stations.scenario: A 55-year-old patient presents with acute onset central chest pain radiating to the left arm, associated with nausea and diaphoresis. BP 90/60, HR 110, O2 sat 94%.
redFlags: Radiation of pain to left arm
rubric: Recognizes red flags and activates STEMI protocol
Orders stat ECG and interprets correctly
Obtains cardiac biomarkers (troponin)
Gives appropriate analgesia (morphine) and antiplatelets (aspirin)
Calls cardiology for emergent PCI evaluation
Manages hypotension appropriately (fluids, inotropes if needed)

stations.scenario: A 28-year-old woman presents with acute dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, and hemoptysis 10 days after a long-haul flight. She is on oral contraceptives. HR 105, RR 24, O2 sat 89% on room air, BP 110/70.
redFlags: Classic triad: dyspnea, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis
rubric: Assesses Wells criteria for PE probability
Orders D-dimer (elevated confirms need for imaging)
Orders CTPA (gold standard for diagnosis)
Starts anticoagulation (LMWH or heparin) empirically if high probability
Assesses for contraindications to thrombolysis
Provides supplemental oxygen and monitors vitals

stations.scenario: A 72-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes presents with sudden-onset right-sided weakness, facial droop, and inability to speak. Symptoms began 90 minutes ago. BP 185/100, HR 88, O2 sat 97%.
redFlags: Acute onset of focal neurological deficits
Time of onset known (<90 minutes — within tPA window)
Aphasia and hemiparesis suggest left MCA territory
rubric: Performs rapid NIH Stroke Scale assessment
Checks blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia
Orders stat non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage
Calculates that patient is within tPA window (3 hours)
Reviews tPA contraindications (recent surgery, bleeding history, etc.)
Manages BP to <185/110 for tPA eligibility
Discusses risks/benefits with patient/family
Administers alteplase if eligible and arranges stroke unit admission

stations.scenario: A 45-year-old with known asthma presents with severe dyspnea, wheezing, and difficulty speaking in full sentences. She has been using her salbutamol inhaler every 2 hours without relief. RR 32, HR 115, O2 sat 87%, PEFR 30% of predicted.
redFlags: Unable to speak in full sentences (severe distress)
rubric: Assesses severity using PEFR, O2 sat, and speaking ability
Administers high-flow oxygen to target SpO2 94-98%
Gives continuous nebulized salbutamol with ipratropium bromide
Administers systemic corticosteroids (IV hydrocortisone or oral prednisolone) within 1 hour
Considers IV magnesium sulfate for severe refractory asthma
Monitors response with serial PEFR measurements
Assesses for signs of life-threatening asthma (silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion)
Arranges ICU admission if poor response or worsening

stations.scenario: A 35-year-old alcoholic presents with hematemesis (bright red blood) and melena. He appears pale and diaphoretic. HR 110, BP 85/60, RR 20, O2 sat 96%. Abdominal exam shows distension and shifting dullness.
redFlags: Active hematemesis suggesting variceal or arterial bleeding
Signs of chronic liver disease (ascites — shifting dullness)
Alcoholism history — high risk for varices
Pallor and diaphoresis suggesting significant blood loss
rubric: Performs ABCDE assessment and starts IV resuscitation
Orders type and crossmatch, CBC, coagulation profile, LFTs
Starts IV fluids and considers blood transfusion (target Hb >7-8)
Administers IV PPI (pantoprazole) empirically
Considers IV ceftriaxone for spontaneous bacterial peritonitis prophylaxis
Administers IV octreotide (somatostatin analog) for suspected variceal bleeding
Arranges urgent upper endoscopy for diagnosis and treatment
Prepares for possible balloon tamponade if massive bleeding

stations.scenario: A 60-year-old hypertensive patient on lisinopril presents to the emergency department with angioedema — swelling of the lips, tongue, and periorbital area with stridor. BP 140/85, HR 95, RR 24, O2 sat 91%.
rubric: Assesses airway urgently — prepares for difficult intubation
Calls anesthesia/ENT for airway evaluation
Discontinues ACE inhibitor immediately and documents allergy
Administers IV antihistamines (diphenhydramine) and corticosteroids
Considers fresh frozen plasma (contains ACE) or icatibant for severe cases
Monitors closely in ICU or high-acuity setting
Educates patient on avoiding all ACE inhibitors and ARBs (cross-reaction risk)
